root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic orientations: downward movement, depression, or depth; and forceful advance to seize or raid.
root_idea.development: The downward branch develops through low land, depth, sinking water, setting celestial bodies, caves, and related forms. A separate branch denotes rapid advance, hostile incursion, and forcible seizure.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural is presented under the supported singular citation form مَغَارَةٌ.

senses.definition: A cave or cavern, especially a hollow in a mountain.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the definite form refers to the cave in which the two companions were sheltered.

senses.definition: Sunken or withdrawn downward into the ground; of water, gone down into the earth.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expressions مَاءٌ غَوْرٌ and أَنْ يُصْبِحَ مَاؤُهَا غَوْرًا, the word describes water that has sunk or gone away into the ground.

senses.definition: A cave or cavern; a hollow or shelter in a mountain.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is plural, مَغَارَاتٍ, and denotes caves or cavernous shelters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or depressed place, especially in a mountain; also a low tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is distinct from the more specific cave sense and may describe a depression or low ground generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go to, travel toward, or journey in a low country or region.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of taking one's way toward the region called the غور, in contrast with elevated land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom contrasting low and high country, to become famous throughout the regions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed tropical expression, not the ordinary physical sense of going to low land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter into a thing, including to enter deeply into it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a physical thing; the construction is distinct from the figurative examination of an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Depth of inquiry or penetration into an affair; figuratively, deep discernment, and in one usage a deeply rancorous or malicious disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of entering or reaching depth; the evaluative meanings are reported as associated applications of بَعِيدُ الغَوْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sun, moon, or a star, to set or disappear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a celestial body passing out of sight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the eye to sink or become depressed into the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression describes a sunken eye and is equated with becoming hollowed or depressed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the day to become intensely hot as the sun declines from the meridian.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed tropical application associated with the heat of midday.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek for or seek after a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object of seeking is expressed directly after the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bestow provisions, benefit, abundance, rain, or means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a person or group as object, often with بِخَيْرٍ, بِرِزْقٍ, or a similar complement; it can also mean to succour with rain or prosperity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bloodwit or compensation paid for a homicide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: غِوَرٌ is also reported as a dialectal variant related to غِيَرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Jealousy, especially jealousy concerning one's spouse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction غَارَ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ expresses being jealous of one's household or spouse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a midday rest, alight for a nap, or travel until midday and then stop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may describe a brief halt for sleep or the action of entering upon and passing through the middle of the day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put or make something enter a low or depressed place; to hide, conceal, or cause it to disappear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use involving lowering or removing something from view.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rout, defeat, put to flight, or drive away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or hostile application of making an opponent withdraw.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away into the country or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This intransitive use is distinct in form from غَارَ meaning to go toward the low country.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or run rapidly and vehemently, especially of a horse or fox.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression can describe pressing forward in walking, marching, journeying, or running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a sudden hostile or predatory incursion or attack against an enemy or a settlement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction أَغَارَ عَلَى takes the enemy, people, territory, or dwellings as its target and may include engagement in conflict.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To plunder or take something by pillage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the transitive result of a hostile incursion and is also used independently.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come to people to aid or succour them, or to come to them seeking aid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The direction and reciprocal relation are expressed by بِ or إِلَى constructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To twist a rope hard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The resulting rope is characterized by the hardness or compactness of its twisting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To marry another woman in addition to one's wife, thereby causing jealousy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional transitive expression concerning a man's household.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make raids or sudden attacks against one another and engage in conflict.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal Form VI construction expresses hostile action between opposing parties or their territories.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To procure provisions or obtain benefit, advantage, or profit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may refer either to acquiring food provisions or to deriving benefit more generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To descend or seek to descend into low land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form can express either actual descent or the desire to reach a low country.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For fat or flesh to enter into, spread through, and become compact in an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported especially of a horse or camel; some descriptions emphasize hardening and compactness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a wound to become swollen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a wound or sore as it rises or becomes enlarged.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or beg God for provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The requested غِيرَة is explained as مِيرَة, provisions of grain or similar food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hole, burrow, or covert to which a wild animal retreats; sometimes a thicket shelter of gazelles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a shelter sense distinct from a cave or cavern in a mountain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The interior of the mouth, including the hollow or upper portion behind the palate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is variously applied to the inner mouth and the paired regions of the palate and lower corresponding area.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sockets or bones in which the eyes are set.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the dual for the paired ocular sockets.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The belly and pudendum, or the mouth and pudendum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional dual expression for two bodily openings or appetites.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An army or a numerous company or body of men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote either a military force or a large assembled group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bay or laurel tree, whose leaves are aromatic and whose fruit and oil are used medicinally or otherwise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun, distinct from the cave sense; it is treated as a noun of unity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The leaves of the grapevine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate botanical application reported for the same form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bottom or lowest part of a thing, and its depth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This direct nominal sense is broader than the Quranic use describing water as sunken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A midday nap or siesta; also the middle of the day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is used for the rest taken at midday and, by extension or usage, for the midday period itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place or direction of sunrise, in an expression for facing east.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed tropical expression describing the orientation of a house or tent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A going away into a country or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or quasi-verbal noun corresponding to the movement expressed by the associated verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A troop of horsemen making a raid or sudden attack.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can denote the raiding force itself, not only the incursion carried out by it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The navel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained as referring to the navel's depth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundance of the produce of the earth, rain, or provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This noun is associated with مِيرَةٌ, provisions, and with bestowed agricultural abundance or rainfall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of entrance, or a place where something is sought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the contrast between entering or seeking in an appropriate place and doing so in an unsuitable one.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of a raid or sudden attack.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A locative noun derived from the hostile-incursion branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse strong or compact in build, especially strong in its joints.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description is figurative, as though the horse were tightly twisted or made compact.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse swift or vehement in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participial noun is applied especially to a horse characterized by rapid movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fighting man, especially one who frequently takes part in raids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related plural may denote raiders or men occupied with repeated incursions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sun.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical noun used as a designation for the sun.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only reference to Forms IV and VI.
Pointer-only reference to the first signification of غَارَ.

cautions: The Quranic plural مَغَارَاتٍ is normalized to the singular dictionary citation form مَغَارَةٌ.
The form غَوْرٌ has a broader Classical sense of depth or low land, but its Quranic occurrences specifically describe water as sunken or gone down into the ground.
